item.title: New TypeScript AMQP 0-9-1 Client Supports Browsers and Node.js
item.description:
New TypeScript AMQP 0-9-1 Client Supports Browsers and Node.js

A new TypeScript client for AMQP 0-9-1 has been released, supporting both Node.js and browsers via WebSocket. Developed and supported by CloudAMQP, the library is designed to replace other Node.js AMQP libraries and enables developers to write browser applications that communicate directly with AMQP servers.

🔍 Overview

The library is Promise-based, integrating well with async/await, and works with any AMQP 0-9-1 broker, including RabbitMQ, LavinMQ, and Apache Qpid. It supports self-hosted instances and managed providers such as CloudAMQP or Amazon MQ, as they all use the same protocol. The codebase is transpiled from TypeScript, and running Node with the --enable-source-maps flag ensures proper stack traces.

🧩 How it works

The library offers two levels of abstraction:

  • High-level (AMQPSession): Provides automatic reconnection and consumer recovery. Users utilize queue() and exchange() handles for reconnect-safe operations.
  • Low-level (AMQPClient / AMQPWebSocketClient): Offers direct channel access with methods such as queueDeclare, basicPublish, and basicConsume.

The transport mechanism is determined by the URL scheme: amqp:// or amqps:// utilizes TCP, while ws:// or wss:// uses WebSocket. To establish a session with automatic reconnection and consumer recovery, developers call AMQPSession.connect(url, options).

⚙️ Key details

The library is secure by default; publishes are not fulfilled until data is sent on the wire or, if Publish Confirms are enabled on the channel, until the server acknowledges that the message has been enqueued.

Message Acknowledgement

  • Messages are acknowledged after the callback returns.
  • If the callback throws, the message is negatively acknowledged (nacked) and requeued.
  • Developers can override this behavior by calling msg.ack() or msg.nack() directly.
  • Subscriptions created via queue.subscribe() are automatically re-established after a reconnection.
  • The sub.consumerTag and sub.channel properties reflect the current consumer and are updated upon reconnection.
  • Prefetch parameters in subscribe settings can be used to configure Quality of Service (QoS) on each connection.

Codec Registry Developers can opt into a codec registry to handle serialization and deserialization based on content-type and content-encoding:

  • Built-in parsers support JSON and text; built-in coders support gzip and deflate.
  • Defaults can be set to avoid repeating configurations on every publish.
  • When codecs are configured, msg.body contains the decoded value; otherwise, it is a Uint8Array. The CodecMode generic infers this type at compile time.
  • Specific publishes can override defaults by passing contentType or contentEncoding in the options.
  • Custom codecs can be registered by merging them with the built-ins.
  • Decode failures surface as a plain Error rather than an AMQPError; in subscribe() contexts, these failures nack the message, honoring requeueOnNack.

#AMQP #TypeScript #WebSockets #RabbitMQ #Messaging #CloudAMQP

Source: cloudamqp/amqp-client.js

item.title: Beep Locator: Using Claude Code to Triangulate a Mysterious Room Beep
item.description:
Beep Locator: Using Claude Code to Triangulate a Mysterious Room Beep

A box‑filled room in a house started emitting an intermittent beep; using Claude Code I built Beep Locator to pinpoint the source.

🔍 Overview

  • The system was created to locate a mysterious beep that began sounding a few weeks ago in a room full of unpacked boxes.
  • Claude Code generated the software, and the solution ran on a Python web server with a browser‑based UI.

🧩 How it works

  • A primary UI is served by a Python web application server.
  • Devices connect to the server via WebSockets after scanning a QR code or opening a URL. The UI requests microphone access.
  • Each listener records a 60‑second buffer of recent audio and runs a simple beep detection algorithm (see detector.js) that applies a Fast Fourier Transform and a high‑pass filter to find potential beeps.
  • When a beep is reported, the server selects the device with the lowest round‑trip time and has it play a short chirp.
  • The server then asks every listener to upload a clip spanning roughly 0.6 s before the beep to 0.8 s after the chirp. The chirp aligns the clips, a crucial step for triangulation.
  • The triangulated locations are plotted on a map; beeps appear as X marks and are logged in a “Sounds located” list.
  • Additional UI features:
    • Rough mode – manually drag device icons to approximate positions, which are then refined using the sound data.
    • Clapping mode – generate test sounds by clapping; these appear as diamonds on the map.

⚙️ Key details

Device Role
Two iPads Listener
Phone Listener
MacBook Pro Listener
Surface Ultra Listener
  • The system measures the interval between beeps and uses the triangulated positions to lock down the most likely source.
  • Reported accuracy was about 40 cm.

📈 Results

  • After the system identified the beep location, digging in the indicated pile of boxes revealed an ancient carbon monoxide detector that needed its batteries replaced.

📚 References

  • While building the project, Claude retrieved the 2007 paper “BeepBeep: A High‑Accuracy Acoustic‑Based System for Ranging and Localization Using COTS Devices.”

#Claude #AcousticLocalization #Python #WebSockets

Source: Locating the source of a mysterious beep with Claude

item.title: Battledrones Gains Four-Player Online Mode and New Compass Rose Map
item.description:
Battledrones Gains Four-Player Online Mode and New Compass Rose Map

On 24 October 2026, the developer added a four‑player online mode to Battledrones, expanding the previous two‑player limit.

🔍 Overview

  • Four‑player online mode added.
  • New map “Compass Rose” with four‑way rotational symmetry.
  • Supports up to four human players via WebSocket non‑audio multiplayer; spare slots filled by AI.
  • New team colors: purple and green, alongside existing blue and red.

🧩 How it works

  • The WebSockets network code was modified to handle up to four connections for the “Compass Rose” map.
  • Players can join using share links or QR codes.
  • If fewer than four human players join, AI opponents fill the remaining slots.

⚙️ Key details

Map Features
Compass Rose Four‑way rotational symmetry, up to four AI players, WebSocket non‑audio multiplayer, join via share link or QR code

🚀 Availability

  • Release date: 24 October 2026.
  • Colors can be previewed in the updated model browser.
  • A replay of a four‑way AI battle with the “Goliath Armada” mutator (each side starts with four giant Goliath mech units) is available.

💡 Why it matters

  • Increases maximum concurrent human players from two to four.
  • Introduces two additional team color schemes, expanding visual variety.
  • Enables flexible multiplayer sessions using share links or QR codes.

#Battledrones #Multiplayer #WebSockets #GameDev

Source: Release: battledrones v14: Compass Rose, a four player map
